# Answer: `generator-shortcuts`

The strongest plausible rival is **fixed two-cell mouth arms**. All four
canonical demonstrations retain exactly two frame-colored cells at each end of
the incomplete side. A rule can therefore ignore the observed gap endpoints,
assume arm lengths 2/2 in every orientation, fill between those assumed tips,
and launch the two yellow diagonals from the assumed tip lines. That rival
matches all 4/4 canonical labels exactly.

An exact lawful input on which it disagrees is the following 7x7 right-open
frame with top/bottom arm lengths 1/3 and shape color 8:

```text
0 0 0 0 0 0 0
8 8 8 8 8 8 0
8 0 0 0 0 0 0
8 0 0 0 0 0 0
8 0 0 0 0 8 0
8 0 0 0 0 8 0
8 8 8 8 8 8 0
```

The intended authority paints yellow from the *actual* one-cell upper arm and
three-cell lower arm. In particular, output cell `(1,6)` is yellow and row 5
inside the frame remains black except for the frame cell. The fixed-2/2 rival
instead leaves `(1,6)` black and paints cells on its incorrectly assumed lower
tip line. Full intended and rival grids are retained in
`repo/generators/bee63e6e52bd/counterexamples/fixed-two-arms.json`.

I generated the input with exact overrides (seed 17, sample index 2, medium,
`scene_profile=7x7`, `open_side=right`, `arm_profile=asym_1_3`, `color=8`) and
ran the pinned Racket rule through `arcpuzzles apply`. The replay report records
rule hash `eedba8f59365`, rule-text SHA
`0a248b89640f86fc27fb84b95ad76431839b7dd3971b992215e8e6c7dbbea8de`,
generator SHA `9ff3ab...cb1`, exact input equality, exact Racket-output equality,
and rival disagreement in `checks/counterexample/replay-summary.json`.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases routinely. Its period-four arm
schedule is `2/2, 1/1, 1/3, 3/1`, so 3 of every 4 default draws refute this
shortcut. The independent probe observed exactly 48 refuting non-2/2 cases in
each 64-draw band sample, and the 300-lesson census found no surviving declared
rival in production order or any of 1,200 query rotations.
